ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Jack makes a cube from 27 small cubes. The small cubes are either grey or white as shown in the diagram. Two small cubes with the same colour are not allowed to be placed next to each other. How many small, white cubes has Jack used?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a large cube made from a 3 by 3 by 3 arrangement of small cubes. The visible small cubes are colored grey and white in an alternating checkerboard pattern. On the visible front face, the four corners and the center are grey, while adjacent visible cubes are white; the top and side faces continue the same alternating pattern. Thus the visible corner parity class is grey. Reasoning: Since the cube is made from 27 small cubes, its positions can be modeled as coordinates (x, y, z) in a 3×3×3 grid, with x, y, z each taking 3 possible values. The rule says that two adjacent cubes cannot have the same color, so the coloring must alternate according to the parity of x + y + z. In a 3×3×3 grid, one parity class contains 14 positions and the other contains 13 positions. Because the diagram shows the corner parity class as grey, grey occupies the larger class of 14 cubes. Therefore the number of white cubes is 27 − 14 = 13.
